title: fix(plugin-auth,plugin-email): the identity import invites with auth.account_invitation, not the password-reset email
body:
Fixes #23343
Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What this changes

Setup › Users › Import (`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/import-users`) invites each email row by asking better-auth for a password reset on that address. So an invited user received `auth.password_reset`: "We received a request to reset the password … If you didn't request this, ignore this email", although they requested nothing. The import's own reset request now sends a new built-in template, **`auth.account_invitation`**. Every other password reset still sends `auth.password_reset`, exactly as before.

This is option A, as the retriage ruled (`6182029999`).

## The new key

| | |
|---|---|
| Name | `auth.account_invitation` |
| Declared in | `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `src/templates/auth-templates.ts`. It is added to `BUILTIN_AUTH_TEMPLATES` (24 rows to 28), which is the plugin manifest's `emailTemplates`, so it is registered exactly as its neighbours are. |
| Locales | `en-US`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`, the set every built-in auth template ships. |
| Exports | `AUTH_ACCOUNT_INVITATION_TEMPLATE`, `AUTH_ACCOUNT_INVITATION_TEMPLATE_ZH_CN`, `_JA_JP`, `_ES_ES`, and the list `AUTH_ACCOUNT_INVITATION_TEMPLATES`: the neighbours' export shape. |
| Spec surface | None. A template name is free dotted snake_case (`email-template.zod.ts`), and `packages/spec` is untouched. |

**Why this name.** It names the event: an account an administrator created for you, and the invitation to set its password. It sits beside `auth.invitation`, which invites an existing person into an organization, as a role, through an accept page. It is not named for the import: any flow that creates an account for someone else and sends a set-password link is the same event. The import is its only sender today.

**Variables.** Declared means filled: the one sender fills exactly these.

| variable | type | required | filled from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user.name` | string | no | the new user's name, else their email (as the reset send does) |
| `user.email` | string | yes | the new user's email |
| `inviter.name` | string | yes | the importing administrator's `sys_user.name`, else their email |
| `inviter.email` | string | yes | the administrator's `sys_user.email`, else the address the platform-admin gate carried |
| `setPasswordUrl` | url | yes | the link better-auth minted. It is the same link as before, landing on the Console's set-password page. |
| `expiresInMinutes` | number | yes | the token's real lifetime (see the TTL section) |
| `appName` | string | no | the deployment's brand name, as in every auth mail |

There is no organization and no role: an imported user on an invite-only or walled deployment has neither (report `6181056129`). The copy says who created the account, for which address, "Set your password", when the link expires, and whom to contact if it has. Its footer is its own, because "if this wasn't you, you can safely ignore this message" fits no invitation. A send missing a required variable is refused with `MISSING_VARIABLES` in every locale.

If no inviter address can be found at all, the row gets the reset copy rather than an invitation with a hole in it, and the import logs one warning. That cannot happen behind the platform-admin gate, whose actor always has a `sys_user` row with an email.

## Where it is selected, and why a public request cannot reach it

**Where.** `sendResetPassword` in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`, because the link exists nowhere else. Measured on the installed better-auth 1.7.3, `dist/api/routes/password.mjs`: `requestPasswordReset` mints the token (`:73`), calls `sendResetPassword({ user, url, token }, ctx.request)` (`:82`–`:86`), and answers only `{ status, message }` (`:87`). The import cannot send the email itself without forking better-auth's mint.

**The marker.** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/account-invitation-marker.ts` (new). `runAsAccountInvitation(marker, fn)` runs the import's own `requestPasswordReset` call inside a fresh better-auth request-state store carrying `{ email, inviter }`. `readAccountInvitation(recipientEmail, request)` reads it inside `sendResetPassword`. better-auth's `auth.api.*` wrapper reuses an open store (`dist/api/to-auth-endpoints.mjs:51`, `if (await hasRequestState()) return run()`), so the endpoint and the callback it calls read that store.

A public `POST /request-password-reset` can never select the new key. Each of the four legs below must hold:

1. **Nothing on the wire writes the marker.** Only `runAsAccountInvitation` sets the slot. Its only caller is the import, behind the platform-admin gate. No body, header or query key reaches it.
2. **Every HTTP request has its own store.** `AuthManager.handleRequest` opens `runWithRequestState(new WeakMap(), …)` for each request, and on Node each store is local to its async context.
3. **The marker is honoured only when `sendResetPassword` receives no `Request`.** better-auth passes `ctx.request`. A probe wrapped the live callback and measured it: a server-side `auth.api.requestPasswordReset({ body })` hands it `undefined`, with or without the marker, and an HTTP `POST /request-password-reset` hands it a `Request`. On the WebContainer polyfill (below), which is process-global, this leg is what still refuses an interleaved public request.
4. **The marker names its recipient.** Only the reset for the address the import invited is re-templated, compared case-insensitively.

If the marker is absent, unreadable or for another address, the send is the `auth.password_reset` call as it was before this PR, line for line.

**The AsyncLocalStorage-across-`await` caveat (H2).** `auth-manager.ts` records that WebContainer's `node:async_hooks` does not carry a store across `await`, and it seeds better-auth's request-state slot with a synchronous polyfill there. So the marker lives in better-auth's own request state rather than in an `AsyncLocalStorage` of its own. It propagates exactly where better-auth's per-request state does: native `AsyncLocalStorage` on Node, and the installed polyfill on WebContainer. There is no runtime on which better-auth's request state works and the marker is lost.

- **Node, native ALS (measured).** The import's send reads the marker across better-auth's user lookup and verification-row write (pin ① below). A task started outside the store does not see it while the marked call is open (unit pin).
- **Polyfill path (measured).** `account-invitation-marker.webcontainer.test.ts` installs the polyfill the way a WebContainer boot does: the `STACKBLITZ` signal, an empty better-auth global, then the `AuthManager` constructor. It asserts the slot is `WebContainerRequestStateAsyncLocalStorage`, then measures three things. The import still sends `auth.account_invitation`. A public reset still sends `auth.password_reset`. The polyfill really is process-global (a task started outside the store reads it), and leg 3 refuses a call that carries a `Request`.
- **Not measured.** A real WebContainer runtime; this container has none. A private `AsyncLocalStorage` of our own would lose the marker there, according to the recorded caveat. That is the design this PR does not take.

The server-held map keyed by email, which the dispatch offered as a fallback, was not needed. It would also race a public reset for the same address on Node, and the request-state design does not.

## The TTL source (H3)

better-auth mints the token with `emailAndPassword.resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn || 3600` seconds (`password.mjs:73`). `sendResetPassword` now states the expiry with the same expression (`|| 60 * 60`, previously `?? 60 * 60`) and passes it to both sends. Pin ⑤ reads the token's own verification row back through `internalAdapter.findVerificationValue`:

- the default gives 3600 s and `expiresInMinutes: 60`;
- a configured 1800 gives 1800 s and 30;
- a configured `0` gives 3600 s and 60.

The `0` case is the only change to what the reset send carries. It used to say "0 minutes" for a 60-minute token.

## What is unchanged

- **`auth.password_reset` and `auth.invitation`:** copy, variables, and the bytes they render, in every locale. The byte-identity pin re-renders all 24 rows that existed before through the registry, and they match their recorded digests.
- **Every reset except the import's own:** same template, same data, same locale ladder (pins ②, ③ and ④).
- **The import's link:** its landing on the Console's set-password page and the origin check on it (`admin-import-users-invite-link.test.ts`, which now reads the new key).
- **`auth-manager.ts`'s catalog reads** (#15194's territory) are not touched. The diff there is one import line plus the `sendResetPassword` region. Inside that region, a comment said the import's reset "reaches this callback with the ADMIN's request". Measured, it reaches it with no request at all, so the comment now says that.
- **H4, registration and serving.** The new key needs no file outside the claimed surface. Measured on a booted `EmailServicePlugin` over a real ObjectQL registry: 28 `email_template` items, and the new key's four rows carry the package id `com.objectstack.service.email`, the same as `auth.password_reset`'s. A Studio save overrides it the way it overrides its neighbours (ADR-0131 D6/D10). The Studio UI list itself was not opened in a browser.

## Tests, at `HEAD` `ad95a1d59`

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-email --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth run typecheck`, then each package's `vitest run --maxWorkers=2`, under the shared verify lock, `VERDICT command-exit 0`:

- `@objectstack/plugin-email`: typecheck `Done`; tests 34 files, 551 passed (515 tests in 33 files at the base).
- `@objectstack/plugin-auth`: typecheck `Done` (test-layer debt unchanged: 10 files, 94 errors, 23 pinned signatures); tests 145 files, 2845 passed and 10 skipped (2829 passed and 10 skipped in 142 files at the base).
- No other package's tests assert the built-in template list. `git grep` for the built-in keys and `BUILTIN_AUTH_TEMPLATES` across all test files finds only these two packages, plus three dogfood files and two spec files that name `auth.password_reset` alone and count nothing.

New and changed pins:

- `plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-account-invitation.test.ts` (new, real ObjectQL over better-sqlite3, a real `AuthManager` with the origin check on, a capturing email service):
  - ① Through the real `POST /admin/import-users` mount, the import sends `auth.account_invitation` with exactly the declared data: the inviter as their `sys_user` row spells them, the set-password link, `expiresInMinutes: 60` and the app name. The token's verification row lives 3600 s, the link lands on the set-password page, and its token sets the password. No `auth.password_reset` reaches the address.
  - ② NEGATIVE CONTROL: a user-requested `POST /request-password-reset` sends `auth.password_reset`, and no invitation is sent at all.
  - ③ After the import, a public reset for the imported address sends `auth.password_reset`. The marker does not leak.
  - ④ While the import's invitation send is held open inside the marker's store, a public reset for the same address runs to completion and sends `auth.password_reset`.
  - ⑤ The TTL source, as above.
  - ⑥ The inviter falls back to the gate's address when the admin has no `sys_user` row. With no address at all, the row gets the reset copy and one warning.
- `plugin-auth/src/account-invitation-marker.test.ts` (new): the four legs against the real request-state storage on Node.
- `plugin-auth/src/account-invitation-marker.webcontainer.test.ts` (new): the polyfill path, as above.
- `plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-invite-link.test.ts`: reads `auth.account_invitation` and `setPasswordUrl`. The token comes from the link's path.
- `plugin-email/src/auth-account-invitation-template.test.ts` (new, independent literals): one registered row per locale, each a valid `EmailTemplateDefinition`. It pins the declared variable list; per locale, the subject, the invitation prose, the inviter, the link (href and plain text), the expiry, the button and the footer, and the absence of every reset phrase; and `MISSING_VARIABLES` for each required variable in each locale, with nothing reaching the transport.
- `plugin-email`: the two built-in list pins go from 24 to 28. The byte-identity pin adds the four new rows' first-render digests, and the other 24 are unchanged. The plain-text-faces pin covers the set-password link.

## Ablation: the marker read

The fix was committed first. `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `const invitation = await readAccountInvitation(user.email, request);` in `auth-manager.ts` with a constant `undefined`. On disk: anchor count 1 to 0, injected marker count 1 inside the run, blob `54472f2b0fac` to `7b60297f0b26`. The subject is imported relatively from `src/`, so no `dist/` is involved.

The run turned red, the expected direction. 9 failed and 9 passed:

- **Red:** account-invitation ①, ③, ④, ⑤ and ⑥; invite-link ① and ②; webcontainer ① and ② (② asserts the address's two mails in order, so it falls with ①).
- **Green:** the NEGATIVE CONTROL ②, the six marker unit pins, the polyfill-installed check, and webcontainer ③.

Restore: the tool's trap put the file back. The blob equals the `HEAD` blob (`54472f2b0fac`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty. `auth-manager.ts` is unchanged since.

## Gates

- **Local.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 commands at `800afa79d` (after merging `origin/main` at `32e03d2fd`). 66 exited 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: it needs every workspace package built, so it is NOT MEASURED locally, and CI runs it.
- **Reconciliation.** `--ran` with the exit-coded record answered `67 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 66 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED`.
- **After the last commit.** That commit, `ad95a1d59`, changed comments only. At `HEAD` these were re-run and exited 0: `node scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs`, `pnpm check:issue-citations`, `pnpm check:doc-authoring`, `pnpm check:nul-bytes`, `node scripts/check-comment-mask-adoption.mjs`, `node scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs`, `node scripts/check-tenant-audit-census.mjs`, `node scripts/check-registry-log-declared.mjs`, `pnpm check:type-check-coverage`, `pnpm check:type-check-debt`, `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `pnpm check:test-source-alias`, and the three changeset gates (`check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-empty-changeset`, each `--base origin/main`).
- **Repo-wide scans.** `pnpm lint` is CI's to run. `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 13 changed TypeScript files exited 0.
- **CI.** The PR's check-runs are cited in the report.

## Acceptance notes

- **File surface.** The marker's definition is its own module, `account-invitation-marker.ts`, rather than a block in `auth-manager.ts`. Both sides (the import writes, `sendResetPassword` reads) import one definition. `auth-manager.ts`'s diff stays at one import line plus the `sendResetPassword` region, and the four legs can be pinned without booting a manager.
- **A failed invitation email is reported as delivered.** This was found and is not part of this PR. Measured at this head: with a transport answering `status: 'failed'`, the import answers 200 with the row `delivery: 'email'`, no `code` and `summary.errors: 0`. better-auth's `runInBackgroundOrAwait` catches and logs what `sendResetPassword` throws (`dist/context/create-context.mjs:215`–`:224`), and `requestPasswordReset` still answers `{ status: true }`. So the import's `INVITE_EMAIL_FAILED` branch is never reached by a delivery failure. This was so before this PR, with the reset template, and it is reported to the seat to file.
- **A spec path better-auth does not serve.** `AuthEndpointPaths.forgetPassword` in `packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts` names `/forget-password`, while better-auth 1.7.3 serves `/request-password-reset`. Nothing outside `packages/spec` in this repo reads `AuthEndpointPaths`. Noted, not filed.
